introduction_markdown: Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1 1/2 hours; you are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II answer EITHER the a, b and c OR the d, e and f of each question. For your guidance the approximate mark(s) for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Non-programmable calculators are allowed.

figures.legende: Two sets of plane waves in a ripple tank: at X an oblique boundary between deep water (left) and shallow water (right); at Y a narrow gap between two barriers.

Le sujet n'imprime pas de total par question : les totaux (`points` de l'exercice) sont la somme des points imprimés bloc par bloc.

Figure 1 : l'ouverture en Y est lue comme une fente étroite (de l'ordre d'une longueur d'onde) : fronts d'onde circulaires attendus après la fente. Le tracé des fronts est demandé à l'élève : il est décrit dans le corrigé, aucune figure de corrigé produite.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Copy each diagram and draw the wave fronts after the obstacle. *[4 marks]*

(ii) Name the wave phenomenon illustrated at X of figure 1. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Obstacle X** (the straight oblique boundary between deep water on the left and shallow water on the right). The waves slow down in the shallow water, so after the boundary:

- the wave fronts are **closer together** (the wavelength is shorter, the frequency is unchanged);
- the wave fronts are **turned** so that the direction of travel bends **towards the normal** to the boundary (the wave fronts become more nearly parallel to the boundary).

Sketch: the incoming straight parallel fronts, then, beyond the line X, a set of straight parallel fronts, more closely spaced and tilted towards the line.

**Obstacle Y** (a narrow gap, about one wavelength wide, between two barriers). The waves are **diffracted** at the gap: after the gap the wave fronts are **circular (semi-circular) arcs** centred on the gap, spreading into the region behind the barriers. The wavelength (spacing of the fronts) stays the same as before the gap.

(ii) At X the phenomenon is **refraction** (a change of speed, and so of direction, when the waves go from deep to shallow water).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define interference. *[1 mark]*

(ii) Two similar waves, each of amplitude 4 cm undergo constructive interference. Determine the amplitude of the resultant wave. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Interference is the **superposition** (overlapping) of two or more waves meeting at a point, the resultant displacement being the sum of the individual displacements.

(ii) In constructive interference the two displacements add in the same direction:

$A = 4\,\mathrm{cm} + 4\,\mathrm{cm} = 8\,\mathrm{cm}$.

**The amplitude of the resultant wave is 8 cm.**
